proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12548 śuṣka explicitly gives northern śukh/šuko, Hindi sūkhā and the -ll extension behind Oriya sukhilā “dry”. This supports simple sūk/sūkhī and l-extended forms; Nepali sukeko is a verbal participle requiring the underlying dry verb to be identified. Reviewed comparator: Buksa sukʰa “dry” (f_idqorou7cmcfg). Any uncertain transfer between Indo-Aryan languages remains open under the user’s preference; source phonetic details are preserved.
